requirement:
The Rust outline profile under {cite}`requirements.references.outlines` MUST
identify items by segments describing their syntactic ancestry within the file,
such as `fn[run]`, `struct[Packet]`, and `mod[local]/fn[run]`, and MUST NOT
resolve Rust modules across files. Functions, methods, structs, enums, unions,
traits, impls, modules, macros, constants, statics, type aliases, and extern
blocks MUST be outline nodes. Impl segments MUST be named by their syntactic self
type and optional trait path, as `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]`. `use`
declarations and other items without a suitable name MUST be anonymous. Selector
spelling MUST be documented.
rationale:
**Implementation.** The Rust profile in `src/outline/rust.rs` carries the `{impl}` markers.

- **Outline nodes.** `KINDS` (lines 129–153) maps every required item kind to an outline node:
  - `function_item` and `function_signature_item` map to `fn`.
  - `struct_item`, `enum_item`, `union_item`, `trait_item` and `mod_item` map to `struct`, `enum`, `union`, `trait` and `mod`.
  - `impl_item` maps to `impl`.
  - `macro_definition` maps to `macro`.
  - `const_item`, `static_item` and `type_item` map to `const`, `static` and `type`.
  - `associated_type` also maps to `type`.
  - `foreign_mod_item` maps to `extern`.
  - `extern_crate_declaration` maps to `extern-crate`.
  - Methods are `function_item` nodes inside `impl_item`, so they are covered too.
- **Ancestry selectors.** Nodes nest by syntactic ancestry through the outline builder. This gives `mod[local]/fn[run]` and `fn[outer]/fn[inner]`.
- **Impl naming.** `impl_name` takes the `type` field and, when present, the `trait` field, both as written. The result is `impl[Thing]` or `impl[Thing/Trait]`. The documented example `impl<T> Trait for Wrapper<T>` becomes `impl[Wrapper<T>/Trait]`.
- **Anonymous nodes.** `use_declaration` is `NameRule::Anonymous`. Item-position `macro_invocation` is also anonymous, gated by `item_macro`/`in_item_list`, so expression macros inside function bodies are not nodes.
- **Extern blocks.** `extern_name` uses the ABI string and falls back to `Rust` when it is absent.
- **No cross-file resolution.** Selectors stay within one file. `mod[external]` is just a node for a `mod x;` declaration.
- **Documentation.** `md/reference.md` documents selector spelling:
  - the "Rust items" section gives examples and the `impl[Wrapper<T>/Trait]` rule;
  - the "Selectors" section covers encoding and duplicate `#N` suffixes;
  - the profile table lists every kind, its grammar nodes and its naming rule.
- **Marking.** I found no implementation of this requirement that lacks an `{impl}` marker. The other items in the file (comment, hash and attach helpers) belong to other requirements and are marked with those.

**Tests.** `src/outline/tests.rs` has three tests that reference the requirement.

- `rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry` checks:
  - all the required kinds, including `union`, `enum`, `const`, `static`, `type`, `macro_rules!`, `extern-crate`, trait `fn` and `type`, and `extern[C]` / `extern[Rust]`;
  - an impl with a non-path self type (`impl[%5Bu8;%204%5D]`), and nested functions;
  - duplicate names (`#1` / `#2`);
  - round-trip resolution of each selector, resolution of the root, and failure on an ambiguous or missing selector.
- `selectors_name_syntactic_ancestry_and_duplicates` checks the same naming rules and also that `use` declarations get distinct anonymous `use@…` selectors.
- `item_macros_are_anonymous_nodes_and_expression_macros_are_not` checks:
  - anonymous item macros at the top level, in an impl and in a mod;
  - that expression macros inside a function body are not nodes;
  - generic impl naming, `impl[Wrapper<T>/Trait]`.

The remaining untested corners are minor: an empty ABI string, and `extern` items inside extern blocks. They are not boundaries the requirement singles out. I found no unacknowledged gaps.

text: :::{req} rust_item_selectors
The Rust outline profile under {cite}`requirements.references.outlines` MUST
identify items by segments describing their syntactic ancestry within the file,
such as `fn[run]`, `struct[Packet]`, and `mod[local]/fn[run]`, and MUST NOT
resolve Rust modules across files. Functions, methods, structs, enums, unions,
traits, impls, modules, macros, constants, statics, type aliases, and extern
blocks MUST be outline nodes. Impl segments MUST be named by their syntactic self
type and optional trait path, as `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]`. `use`
declarations and other items without a suitable name MUST be anonymous. Selector
spelling MUST be documented.
:::{req} outlines
Habeas MUST parse Rust, Python, TypeScript, CSS, Markdown, TOML, and YAML
sources with pinned tree-sitter grammars, selected by file extension compared
case-insensitively. A source with any syntax error MUST fail to parse, reporting
the line of its first error. Every
other text file MUST use a plain-text profile in which each line that is not
blank is an anonymous outline node of kind `line`. Each supported language MUST
have an outline profile that maps grammar node kinds to short outline kind names
and, for each mapped kind, states whether a node is named, and by which fields
or children, or anonymous. Only mapped kinds MUST appear in the outline; other
nodes MUST be transparent, so their outline descendants appear under the
nearest outline ancestor. A profile MAY attach grammar siblings to an outline
node, such as Rust attributes and doc comments preceding an item, so the outline
tree need not match the grammar tree exactly; attached siblings are part of that
node for its line range and hash. Every file's outline MUST have a root node
for the whole file, independent of language. Source in no other outline node,
such as top-level statements no profile maps, MUST belong to the root node;
profiles MUST NOT invent fallback kinds for it. Comments MUST NOT be outline nodes. Profiles MUST be
documented. Upgrading a grammar or profile MAY change outlines and MUST be
treated as a deliberate change.
